net/endpoint#

Where to connect: a host name or an address, and a port.

Version: v1.0.0

Synopsis#

let site = HostEndpoint(HostName("bücher.example"), 443);
site.host().ascii();                  // "xn--bcher-kva.example"
let local = IpEndpoint(IpAddress("127.0.0.1"), 8080);

Description#

Where to connect: a host name or an address, and a port.

HostName checks the name and keeps its ASCII (IDNA) and Unicode forms.

object IpEndpoint#

object IpEndpoint

Immutable numeric endpoint. Construction performs no DNS, interface lookup, service lookup or socket I/O. The original IpAddress stays undecorated. Ports are 0..65535. Zero represents an OS-assigned bind request; a consuming connect/send operation must reject it when a destination port is required.

IpEndpoint(IpAddress("fe80::1"),443,"eth0").string();
// "[fe80::1%eth0]:443"

Empty zone means absent. Nonempty zones require IPv6 and ASCII letters, digits or -._~. This portable spelling subset preserves case/leading zeros; it does not assert that the interface exists. Numeric zones stay strings. string() is endpoint display text with a literal %, not a URI serializer. Validation reports InvalidPort before InvalidIpv6Zone if both are invalid.
